sentences.text: Chinchenia is an extinct basal pistosauroid from the Middle Triassic of Guizhou Province in southwestern China.
This reptile belongs to the class Reptilia.
The genus is known from at least four extremely fragmentary individuals that were preserved and collected together.
The genus was first described by Yang Zhongjian, also known as Chung-Chien Young, in 1965.
Fossils were collected near the Cangxi Bridge at Shangpu, Tsanchichiao, 7 km west of Qingzhen in Guizhou Province.

The lectotype specimen is IVPP V3227, consisting of the front end of the left mandible, while paratypes include jaw parts with teeth, vertebrae, ribs, shoulder bones, arm bones, leg bones, and a fibula fragment. All known Chinchenia specimens are housed at the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology.
The parent group of Chinchenia is Pistosauroidea.
While originally attributed to the Anisian Guangling Formation, subsequent authors considered a Ladinian age more likely for the material.
